body_markdown:
Restoration software is job-management software for water, fire and mold companies: it holds the job file, photos, moisture readings and drying logs, schedules crews and equipment, tracks customers and referral sources, and stores the documents insurers ask for. It runs the job once it exists. The job usually starts as a phone call, often at night — which is where an AI answering service fits.


The[restoration answering service](https://sameday.ai/industries/restoration) page covers trade-specific call handling. For marketplace lead rules, see[Thumbtack vs Angi](https://sameday.ai/post/thumbtack-vs-angi) . For the free listing that sends many of those calls, see[Google Business Profile for contractors](https://sameday.ai/post/google-business-profile-for-contractors) . For who answers when the PM is on site, see[virtual assistant for contractors](https://sameday.ai/post/virtual-assistant-for-contractors) .


## What restoration job management software does


Restoration job management software is built around one job file per loss. The category typically covers:


- Job files and documentation — photos, video, notes and compliance paperwork with timestamps
- Moisture mapping and drying logs — readings, equipment placement and dry-out progress for water losses
- Equipment tracking — dehumidifiers, air movers and other gear tied to rooms or phases
- Scheduling and dispatch — crews, on-call rotations and multi-location boards
- Time tracking — often mobile, sometimes geo-fenced to the job site
- CRM and referral tracking — plumbers, agents, adjusters and repeat customers
- Estimates and job costing — labor, subs and materials against the original scope
- Mobile apps — field capture that syncs back to the office without a phone tag


Those jobs are why shops buy restoration software. They are not the same job as answering at 2 a.m. during a freeze break or a storm surge.


### Mold remediation software


Mold remediation software, in practice, is usually the same restoration platform with workflows tuned for containment, documentation and clearance testing. Shops need photos, schedules and paperwork stored in one place; check each vendor's own page for mold-specific steps rather than assuming a separate product category.


### Restoration CRM


Restoration CRM work inside these platforms means referral partners, insurance contacts and homeowners in one record — who sent the job, claim status, and follow-up on inspections. The CRM stores the relationship after someone has already made contact. The first contact is still often a phone call.

### DASH (Cotality)


[DASH](https://www.cotality.com/products/dash) is Cotality's job management platform for restoration contractors, formerly DASH by Next Gear Solutions. Cotality lists centralized job management, custom workflows and automated tasks, photo and video job files with timestamps, Cotality property data that auto-populates address details, compliance and document storage, and iOS and Android apps. Cotality's property-restoration materials also list CRM workflows in DASH and a separate[Restoration CRM](https://www.cotality.com/products/restoration-crm) product. This page does not claim that Sameday integrates with DASH.


### Albi (Albiware)


[Albi](https://www.albiware.com/) groups restoration work into job management, customer management and business operations on one platform. Albiware lists photo documentation, moisture mapping, a mobile scheduler, e-signatures, equipment scanning, a timeclock, staff inbound answer/hold/transfer in its call tools, call tracking and recording on its Pro tier, and an early-access[Lead Taker](https://help.albiware.com/ai-agents#lead-taker) AI assistant that answers calls and collects job details. This page does not claim that Sameday integrates with Albi.


### Xcelerate


[Xcelerate](https://www.xlrestorationsoftware.com/) describes an all-in-one restoration job management platform. On[Explore Xcelerate](https://www.xlrestorationsoftware.com/explore-xcelerate) , Xcelerate lists dynamic workflows, scheduling and dispatch, geo-fenced time tracking tied to job costing, CRM with referral tracking, multi-location dashboards, and mobile field capture. Its[water damage restoration](https://www.xlrestorationsoftware.com/water-damage-restoration) page lists moisture readings, drying logs, equipment tracking, generating task lists, assigning technicians, and tracking work orders. This page does not claim that Sameday integrates with Xcelerate.


## What restoration software doesn't do: the first call


Restoration software starts after someone has decided to call your company. The water-loss call at 2 a.m., the storm surge that rings five lines at once, the mold inspection request, and the adjuster who needs a status update all hit the phone first.


Intake on that call usually needs address, source of loss, whether water is still active, whether the caller has a carrier and claim number, adjuster timing, and whether the loss meets your emergency rules. None of that is automatic just because you bought a job-management platform.


Drying logs start after someone answers and dispatches the first crew.


## Where call answering fits next to your restoration software


Restoration answering is the layer that turns a ring into a job file entry your software can use. From the[restoration answering service](https://sameday.ai/industries/restoration) page, that work includes:


- Answering 24/7, including spikes and storm surges, with multiple calls handled in parallel when volume jumps
- Asking your intake questions and applying your emergency rules
- Transferring the on-call project manager with a summary when the loss is a true emergency
- Booking inspections for the rest, with addresses checked against your service area
- Capturing carrier, claim number, deductible and adjuster timing and writing those fields into ServiceTitan or Housecall Pro on a booked call

## Restoration software + call intake checklist


Seven checks for restoration software plus intake


1.


After-hours calls answered?


Call your main number at 2 a.m. and during a storm cell. Note who picks up — a person, a recording, or nothing.


2.


Emergency criteria written down?


List what counts as a true emergency versus a next-day inspection. Everyone on call should match the same list.


3.


On-call PM transfer tested?


Place a test emergency call and confirm the on-call project manager receives address and summary, not just a blinking number.


4.


Insurance fields captured on the call?


On a claim-style scenario, confirm carrier and claim number are asked before the caller hangs up.


5.


Booking lands in your system during the call?


Watch ServiceTitan or Housecall Pro while the test call is still open. A job that arrives later in email is not a booking on the call.


6.


Storm-day overflow plan?


Know how parallel calls are handled when five lines ring at once. Sameday can answer multiple calls at once; your restoration platform still needs one job file per loss.


7.


Call recordings disclosed per state law?


If calls are recorded, follow your state's disclosure rules before you turn recording on.

## FAQ


### What is restoration software?


Restoration software is job-management software built for water, fire and mold restoration companies. It typically holds the job file, photos, moisture readings and drying logs, schedules crews and equipment, tracks customers and referral sources, and stores the documentation insurers ask for.


### What does water damage restoration software do?


It documents each water loss from first visit to final dry-out: photos and video with timestamps, moisture mapping and drying logs, equipment placed, crew schedules, and the documents needed for the insurance claim. Most platforms include mobile apps for technicians.


### What is mold remediation software?


Mold remediation companies typically use the same restoration job-management platforms to document the area, track the work and store photos and paperwork. Some platforms list mold-specific workflows; check each vendor's page.


### What is DASH restoration software?


DASH is Cotality's job management platform designed for restoration contractors, formerly DASH by Next Gear Solutions. Cotality lists custom workflows, photo and video job files with timestamps, property data that fills in address details, document storage and mobile apps ([cotality.com](https://www.cotality.com/products/dash) ).


### What is Albi restoration software?


Albi, from Albiware, is restoration management software. Its site lists photo documentation, moisture mapping and drying logs, a mobile scheduler, equipment scanning, a timeclock, e-signatures and a CRM ([albiware.com](https://www.albiware.com/) ).


### Does restoration software answer the phone?


Mostly no. Restoration software runs the job after it exists. Some platforms list call tracking or recording. An AI answering service answers the call itself, 24/7, asks your intake questions, transfers true emergencies to the on-call project manager and books inspections.


### Does Sameday integrate with restoration software?


Sameday's confirmed integrations named on this page are ServiceTitan (Certified ServiceTitan app) and Housecall Pro. On a booked call, Sameday writes the customer and the job into the software, including insurance fields like the carrier and claim number. This page does not claim integrations with DASH, Albi or Xcelerate.
